comment: posixregex.c regex_match() on non-ASCII text: NetHack never calls setlocale(), so glibc's regexec() runs in the C locale and treats each UTF-8 byte as a character. With eight_bit_tty the fruit name keeps its two-byte e-acute, so in the O menu's fruit line "\[caf..\]" matches (red, underlined) and "\[caf.\]" does not, the reverse of a UTF-8 locale. Seed, date, Healer and fruit chosen independently.
